descripcion_es: Actions happening now and temporary situations.
resumen: The present continuous (am/is/are + verb in -ing) describes what is happening at this moment or in this period, in contrast with the present simple, which expresses habits.

explicacion.texto: It is formed with the present of to be and the verb ending in -ing: I am reading (es: estoy leyendo). It is used for actions in progress now (now, at the moment, right now) and for temporary situations (this week, these days).

filas: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.

items: Spelling: most verbs add -ing (play, playing); a final -e is dropped (make, making); a short stressed syllable with consonant + vowel + consonant doubles the consonant (run, running; sit, sitting); -ie changes to -ying (lie, lying).
Present simple = habit (I walk to work); present continuous = now or temporary (I'm taking the bus this week).
State verbs such as like, love, want, know, need or understand are almost never used in the continuous: I know (not “I'm knowing”).

ejemplos.frase: Be quiet, the baby is sleeping.
I'm reading a very good book at the moment.
ejemplos.traduccion: Estoy leyendo un libro muy bueno estos días.

ejemplos.frase: They aren't watching TV, they're playing cards.
ejemplos.traduccion: No están viendo la tele, están jugando a las cartas.

ejemplos.frase: My sister is staying with us this week.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mi hermana se está quedando con nosotros esta semana.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: For what is happening at this moment, use the continuous.
Want is a state verb and is not usually used in the continuous.
You cannot leave out the auxiliary to be.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: We are siting in the park.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: We are sitting in the park.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the present continuous.
ejercicios.explicacion: The basic rule of the card applies: the present continuous is formed with am/is/are + verb in -ing and is used for actions in progress now. The clue is Listen!, which tells us the singing is happening as we speak. Someone is third person singular, so it needs is. The result is is singing (or the contraction 's singing); sing just adds -ing, with no spelling changes.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¡Escucha! Alguien está cantando en la calle.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The present simple expresses habits; here the action is happening at this moment (Listen!), so you need is singing.
The verb be is missing: in English -ing alone does not form the tense. It must be is singing.
Someone is singular and agrees with is, not with are.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the present continuous.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's rule is am/is/are + -ing for an action in progress, and right now makes it clear. The subject we needs are. Have is normally a state verb when it means “possess”, but here it means “eat” (have lunch); it is an action and can be used in the continuous. Also, by the spelling rule, the final -e is dropped: have → having. The answer is are having or 're having.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Have meaning “eat” can be continuous; the e is dropped: having.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The final -e of have disappears when you add -ing: having.
Right now needs the present continuous, not the present simple: are having.
With we the auxiliary is are, not is.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the present continuous.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's spelling rule applies: when the verb has a short stressed syllable ending in consonant + vowel + consonant, the last consonant is doubled before -ing. Swim ends in i + m, so it becomes swimming. The subject The children is plural (they) and needs are. The action is happening now, so it goes in the present continuous: are swimming or 're swimming.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los niños están nadando en la piscina.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The m must be doubled: swim has consonant + vowel + consonant and becomes swimming.
The children is plural: the auxiliary is are.
The sentence describes what is happening now; you need are swimming.

ejercicios.frase: I ___ (not / work) this week. I'm on holiday.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the use for temporary situations that the card includes: this week marks a limited period, not a habit. The negative is formed by putting not after the verb be: with I it is I'm not or I am not + -ing. So the answer is 'm not working (contracted) or am not working. Note that the contraction “amn't” does not exist; the contracted form with I is always I'm not.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With I the negative is I'm not + -ing.
ejercicios.traduccion: Esta semana no estoy trabajando. Estoy de vacaciones.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the Spanish present; for a temporary situation (this week) you need the continuous: I'm not working.
After be + not the verb must take -ing: working.
The verb be is missing: I'm not working.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card says the present continuous is used for what is happening at this moment. The clue is Look!, which draws attention to something happening in front of us. The bus is third person singular, so the form is is coming. Note that in Spanish we say “viene” in the simple present, but English requires the continuous for an action in progress.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Look! shows it is happening now.

por_opcion.comes: This is the present simple and would express a habit (The bus comes every ten minutes); it does not work for something happening right now.
por_opcion.is coming: Correct: is + coming describes the action in progress that Look! points to. Coming drops the -e of come.
por_opcion.come: This is the base form, without -s or be; it does not agree with the bus and does not express an action in progress.

ejercicios.explicacion: Here the contrast in the card applies: present simple = habit; present continuous = now or temporary. The clue is every day, which shows a routine. So the correct form is the present simple walk, which takes no -s with I. The continuous am walking would only make sense for a temporary situation (I'm walking to work this week).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Every day expresses a habit: present simple.
ejercicios.traduccion: Voy andando al trabajo todos los días.

por_opcion.walk: Correct: present simple for a habit marked by every day; with I there is no -s.
por_opcion.am walking: This is the present continuous; it is for what is happening now or temporarily, not for a daily routine.
por_opcion.walking: An -ing form alone, without subject + be, does not form any tense in English.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card's rule on state verbs applies: like, love, want, know, need or understand are almost never used in the continuous, because they describe a state, not an action in progress. Know is one of them, so even though we are talking about the present moment, we use the present simple. With she, third person, the verb takes -s: knows.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Know is a state verb and goes in the present simple.

por_opcion.is knowing: Incorrect: know is a state verb and is not used in the present continuous.
por_opcion.knows: Correct: present simple of a state verb, with the third-person -s.
por_opcion.know: It is missing the third-person singular -s that she requires.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card shows that a question in the present continuous is formed by inverting be and the subject: (question word) + am/is/are + subject + -ing. The clue is doing, which shows the sentence is in the continuous, and the subject you, which requires are. So: What are you doing?. Do would be the auxiliary of the present simple, which is never followed by a verb in -ing.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Continuous question with you: are + subject + -ing.

por_opcion.do: Do is the auxiliary of the present simple (What do you do?, es: ¿a qué te dedicas?); it cannot go with doing.
por_opcion.are: Correct: are agrees with you and, with doing, forms the question in the present continuous.
por_opcion.is: Is goes with he/she/it; with you you must use are.

ejercicios.explicacion: According to the card's table, in a question the verb be goes before the subject: Are you working today?. Applied to He is driving, is goes before he and the rest stays the same: Is he driving?. Do or does is not added, because the continuous already has its own auxiliary (be). Driving drops the -e of drive.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The auxiliary is and the subject change places.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Intonation alone is not enough in written English: you must invert the auxiliary and the subject.
The present continuous does not use does; the auxiliary is is, which goes before the subject.
The -ing has been lost: the question keeps driving.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card shows the negative with They aren't listening: not is added after the verb be and the main verb keeps the -ing. Three forms are accepted: the full form They are not listening and two contractions, They aren't listening and They're not listening, which mean the same. Don't is not used, because this tense is not formed with do.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Mixed tenses: the present continuous makes the negative with be + not, not with don't.
The verb be is missing: They aren't listening.
The main verb must keep the -ing: listening.

ejercicios.explicacion: The mistake is a spelling one, and the card covers it: when the verb ends in -e, the e is dropped when you add -ing. Make becomes making, not makeing. The rest of the sentence is correct: she + is + -ing for an action in progress. The contracted form She's making a cake is also accepted.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: makeing is misspelt; it must be making.
Make does not double the consonant: it simply drops the -e and becomes making.
This changes the meaning to a habit; the mistake was only in the spelling, and writing making is enough.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card's rule on state verbs applies: like expresses a liking, which is a state and not an action in progress, so it is not used in the continuous. Although in Spanish we might think “me está gustando”, in English the normal form is the present simple: I like this song. Note: the famous slogan “I'm loving it” is an expressive advertising use, not the rule.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Like is a state verb: present simple.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: like is a state verb and is not used in the continuous.
With I the present simple takes no -s: I like.
The verb be is not needed: the present simple is formed with the verb alone, I like.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that in questions the verb be goes before the subject. With a question word the order is Why + are + you + -ing. In the original sentence the subject comes first (you are), which is the order of a statement and a calque of Spanish “¿por qué tú estás…?”. The correct form is Why are you laughing?.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In a question the auxiliary goes before the subject.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: in the question are must go before you.
The continuous does not use do; the auxiliary is are: Why are you laughing?
The verb must keep the -ing: laughing.

respuestas: My brother is writing a letter
Is my brother writing a letter
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives the order of the affirmative: subject + am/is/are + verb in -ing + object. The subject is my brother, then is and then writing a letter. As the words have no punctuation, the question is also accepted, with is before the subject: Is my brother writing a letter. Writing drops the -e of write.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi hermano está escribiendo una carta. (También: ¿Está escribiendo mi hermano una carta?)

errores_previstos.respuesta: My brother writing is a letter
errores_previstos.explicacion: The auxiliary is must go just before the verb in -ing: is writing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My brother is a letter writing
errores_previstos.explicacion: This order is copied from other languages: in English the object goes after the verb.

descripcion_larga_es: The present continuous (am/is/are + verb in -ing) tells what is happening right now or during a temporary period. It is similar to Spanish “estar + gerundio”, but English uses it more strictly: habits go in the present simple, and state verbs (know, like, want) are almost never used in the continuous. Spanish speakers find it hard to remember the verb be, the spelling of -ing and the word order in questions.

contexto.que_es: It is the tense formed with the present of to be (am, is, are) and the main verb ending in -ing: She is cooking. It shows that an action is in progress at the moment of speaking or that a situation is temporary.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is essential for describing what is happening around you, a picture or a temporary situation, which is very common in any oral exam. Confusing it with the present simple changes the meaning: I work here (regularly) is not the same as I'm working here (for now). Mistakes in form (She cooking, makeing) are very noticeable even at basic levels.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is required by markers such as now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, these days, or exclamations such as Look! and Listen!. It is also used to describe photos and scenes. Spanish speakers tend to use it with state verbs (I'm knowing, I'm liking), to leave out be and to keep the subject before the auxiliary in questions (Why you are…?).
